Diagnosis: set_key (main.py:184-185) escapes only apostrophes when single-quoting, leaving literal backslashes unescaped. The parser (parser.py:25,32,132) decodes single-quoted values via codecs unicode-escape, so `\n`/`\\` get transformed and a trailing lone backslash breaks the closing-quote match — corrupting consecutive backslashes and apostrophes.

Plan: In set_key's quoting branch, escape backslashes first, then apostrophes: value_to_set.replace("\\","\\\\").replace("'","\\'"). This lets the parser's `\\`→`\` and `\'`→`'` decode reproduce the exact value. Preserve quote_mode selection, export, and never behavior. Add round-trip tests for consecutive backslashes and apostrophes under always/auto using dotenv_values(interpolate=False).
